items.title: Characterization of geometric connectedness by connectedness after every finite separable field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a scheme X over a field k is geometrically connected if and only if X_{k'} is connected for every finite separable extension k'/k (statement lines 935-945). One direction is immediate from the definition. For the other, the author assumes X_{\bar k} disconnected with a decomposition into two open and closed nonempty pieces (proof lines 947-955), then manufactures a decomposition over a finite subextension: for every quasi-compact open W the two pieces of W_{\bar k} are quasi-compact and defined over a finite subextension and invariant under an open subgroup of the Galois group (proof lines 957-968), after which the intersection over that open subgroup and the union over it produce open and closed subsets U_W and V_W of W_{\bar k} (proof lines 985-1001), and these glue over all W into a decomposition of X_{\bar k} that is invariant under an open subgroup, hence descends to a finite separable extension (proof lines 1002-1017). The claim is H2: the Galois-descent bookkeeping with open subgroups is the non-formal content, while every individual input is a standard statement about the absolute Galois group.
